issues.failure_explanation: The text asserts that as $h_{\max}\to0$ (with $R$ fixed) the two-sided bounds \eqref{eq:bounds} converge to $\lambda_k$. In the limit $h\to0$ the upper bound tends to $\lambda_k^R\ge\lambda_k$ (Dirichlet truncation, strictly larger in general) and the lower bound tends to $\mu_k^{R,N}(1-\lambda_k^R/\sigma(R))$, which is strictly below $\mu_k^{R,N}$ by the factor $\lambda_k^R/\sigma(R)>0$. Hence at fixed $R$ the enclosure width converges to a positive quantity (at least $\mu_k^{R,N}\lambda_k^R/\sigma(R)$ plus the Dirichlet truncation gap), not to zero; convergence to $\lambda_k$ additionally requires $R\to\infty$.

failure_location.quote: so the bounds converge to the true eigenvalues.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as convergence when both $h_{\max}\to0$ and $R\to\infty$ (noting $\sigma(R)\to\infty$ and $\lambda_k^R,\mu_k^{R,N}\to\lambda_k$), or state that at fixed $R$ the bounds converge to $\lambda_k^R$ and $\mu_k^{R,N}(1-\lambda_k^R/\sigma(R))$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence property of the method is false as written; the rigorous enclosures themselves remain valid, but the advertised asymptotic behaviour is misdescribed.
issues.title: Bounds do not converge to true eigenvalues as h→0 at fixed R
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence local correction of the limit statement fixes the claim; no rigorous result or guarantee of the paper depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
so restricting $u_k$ to $D(R)$ and computing its Rayleigh
  quotient with respect to $a_{D(R)}$ gives

issues.failure_explanation: Two gaps. (i) The Rayleigh quotient of the single function $u_k|_{D(R)}$ only bounds $\mu_1^{R,N}$ (or $\mu_k$ if a $k$-dimensional trial space is used); the remark does not use the span of $u_1,\dots,u_k$, so the inference $\mu_k^{R,N}\le\lambda_k+O(e^{-\alpha R})$ is not justified as written. (ii) More substantively, the claimed absolute bound $|\mu_k^{R,N}-\lambda_k|\le C_k'e^{-\alpha_k'R}$ requires an exponentially small lower bound $\mu_k^{R,N}\ge\lambda_k-Ce^{-\alpha R}$. Neither the Agmon Rayleigh-quotient argument (which gives only an upper bound on $\mu_k^{R,N}$) nor Proposition~\ref{prop:neumann} (which also yields only $\mu_k^{R,N}\le\lambda_k/(1-\Lambda_k/\sigma(R))$, an algebraic upper bound) provides any lower bound on $\mu_k^{R,N}$. The 'Combined with Proposition' step therefore does not establish the two-sided estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the remark to the one-sided statement $\mu_k^{R,N}\le\lambda_k+O(e^{-\alpha R})$ (proved via the restricted span of $u_1,\dots,u_k$) together with the algebraic lower control from Proposition~\ref{prop:neumann}, or add a separate argument (e.g. an IMS-type localization) for the exponential lower bound on $\mu_k^{R,N}$.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential-accuracy claim for the Neumann truncation, and the consequent statement that $\nu_{k,h}^{R,N}(\overline V)$ are accurate approximations converging exponentially in $R$, are unsupported as written. The rigorous bounds \eqref{eq:bounds} are unaffected, as the paper itself notes.
issues.title: Two-sided exponential Neumann estimate in Remark agmon is not established by the given argument
issues.why_classification: The remark is explicitly heuristic and is not used in any rigorous bound; a local weakening of the stated estimate resolves the defect without loss to the paper's substantive guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For $V_1$ the $O(2)$ symmetry produces degenerate eigenvalue
pairs.  Both features are confirmed by the rigorous bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark offers identical two-sided bounds as the proof of degeneracy. Two eigenvalues lying in the same interval $[3.72649,3.89427]$ (width 4.5%) are not thereby shown to be equal; the computed enclosures are compatible with $\lambda_2<\lambda_3$. Degeneracy of $|m|\ge1$ modes follows from the $O(2)$ symmetry, but the bounds neither prove this nor rigorously identify $k=2,3$ (resp. $4,5$) as the $|m|=1$ (resp. $|m|=2$) modes; the intro's statement that this is 'confirmed by the rigorous bounds' is likewise unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'provably degenerate (identical bounds)' by a statement that the bounds are consistent with the symmetry-induced degeneracy, or supply a symmetry/angular-momentum argument identifying the modes.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the computed bounds prove or confirm degeneracy is unsupported; the numerical enclosures themselves remain valid.
issues.title: Identical enclosures do not prove degeneracy of λ2, λ3 (and λ4, λ5)
issues.why_classification: A local rewording removes the false inference; no rigorous result depends on it.

issues.title: Error-source attribution contradicted by the reported data
issues.why_classification: Purely a misstatement in the discussion of numerical results; correcting the figures requires no change to any method, proof, or guarantee.
